name: get_status
description: Status of the bridge itself, not of a page: call it when a tool you expect is missing or browser commands fail (connected=false: the extension is not reachable, extension_install gives its Chrome Web Store link). Also reports mode (primary/relay), host, port, server and extension versions, js_evaluation (false under --no-js), write_root, read_root, session_tab_id (the implicit tab), owned_tabs (created by this session), uptime_sec, webmcp (whether WebMCP is active in the session tab, and how to enable it). caps_active and caps_available: a missing tool lives in an inactive cap. enable is the only change it makes: it switches caps on for this session, no restart, and lists the tools added. Optional caps: audits (cookie_audit); visual (inject_css, measure_spacing, emulate_media, viewport_resize); perf (animations, frames, perf_trace, screencast, lighthouse, heap_snapshot); network (http_auth, set_geolocation, track_events); storage (get_storage, set_storage, session_fixture); dom (modify_dom, watch_dom, drag_and_drop); files (save_page, manage_downloads, session_record).

enable.description: Caps to switch on now, all in one call; "all" = every cap

name: get_tabs
description: List every open tab with id, url, title, active flag and mine (created by this session). Find a tab_id when the implicit target is not the one you mean. include_windows adds position, size, state and type of each window — needed before moving or tiling. Session tabs gone since the last call come back once in closed_session_tabs with the reason (closed, window_closed, replaced, closed_by_bridge).

include_windows.description: Also return the windows with bounds, state, type and tab count

name: navigate
description: Navigate a Chrome tab to a URL and wait for the load; DNS and connection errors fail the call. Without tab_id it reuses the tab this session last navigated or created, else opens a new one rather than taking over the active tab. Returns a preview of interactive elements with refs usable in click/type_text/hover, plus the first console errors and failed requests, if any, and the WebMCP tools the page declares.

url.description: Absolute URL, or a path resolved against the current page

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: screenshot
description: Screenshot of the visible viewport only (PNG), at the current scroll position, or one per viewport preset with presets. Read-only. Activates the tab in the background without stealing window focus, then restores the previous tab. Downscaled to ≤1568px: for fine print, element_screenshot with scale.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

save_to.description: Absolute path: write the PNG there and return the path instead of the content

presets.description: Resizes the window per preset, then restores it; not phone emulation. A refused width is reported, not shot. save_to = directory

if_changed.description: Same pixels as the last screenshot of this tab: a note instead of the image. false = always send it

name: execute_js
description: Run JavaScript in the page (MAIN world). Requires the extension's "Allow user scripts" toggle; errors explain setup if disabled. Use it when no dedicated tool fits: extract or extract_table read data, query_dom inspects elements, inject_css restyles, and none of them needs the toggle. A promise is awaited up to timeout. A cut result stays valid JSON and says truncated; save_to writes the whole result to disk.

code.description: JS evaluated in the page; the value of the last expression is returned

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

timeout.description: Max ms to wait for the result (default 30000); raise it for long async work

save_to.description: Absolute path: write the result (a string as is, anything else as JSON) there and return the path instead of the content

name: click
description: Click an element by CSS selector or by a ref (n1, n2…) from get_interactives or navigate. A real pointer sequence: it can submit, open a dialog or navigate — use wait_after. Not idempotent; a native confirm() blocks the bridge: handle_dialogs first. Returns page_changed (url, title and DOM deltas: nodes, text, open, expanded, checked, dialogs, focus): the effect, without a screenshot; when the click opens or reveals something, the refs of the visible interactives follow, no get_interactives needed.

selector.description: CSS selector; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM. Ignored when ref is given

button.description: right opens the page context menu instead of activating the element

count.description: 2 emits dblclick after the two clicks, which is what selects a word or opens an editor

trusted.description: Real browser input (isTrusted) via chrome.debugger, main frame only: for widgets that ignore synthetic clicks

wait_after.description: Settle before returning: navigation waits for a page load, networkidle for quiet traffic

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

name: type_text
description: Put text into an input, textarea or contenteditable, by selector or ref. Replaces the whole value through the native setter (React/Vue controlled inputs register it) and fires input and change. mode=keys emits keydown/input/keyup per character for autocomplete and masked fields: slower, use it only when mode=set leaves the field empty. Returns value_after; mismatch=true means the field did not keep the value: retry with mode=keys.

selector.description: CSS selector; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM. Ignored when ref is given

text.description: Value to type; empty string clears the field

mode.description: set = assign value; keys = per-char events (autocomplete/masked); trusted = real input via chrome.debugger, main frame

wait_after.description: Settle before returning: navigation waits for a page load, networkidle for quiet traffic

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

name: read_page
description: Read the page as text (default), markdown, raw HTML, or accessibility tree. Read-only. markdown keeps headings, links and tables at a fraction of the HTML cost. Expensive on big pages: HTML on a large table costs tens of thousands of tokens for data you filter anyway — prefer extract_table/extract for repeated content, get_interactives for click targets.

mode.description: text strips markup; markdown keeps headings/links/tables far cheaper than html; accessibility = a11y tree

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

name: get_page_info
description: Page metadata: title, url, visibility, doctype, charset, meta tags, scripts, stylesheets, links and forms. visibility=hidden means the window is minimized, covered or in the background: the page does not render (screenshots fail) and its timers slow down. dev.server names a dev server (vite, webpack-dev-server, next, nuxt) and dev.overlay carries the compiler message when an error overlay is open: read it before treating the page as valid. For the text use read_page, for specific elements query_dom, for the bridge itself get_status.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

name: get_storage
description: Read localStorage, sessionStorage or cookies of the current origin (type=all for every one). Read-only. Cookies come with domain, path, expiry and the httpOnly/secure flags, so this also answers whether a session cookie is present — write them back with set_storage, or snapshot a logged-in state with session_fixture.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: query_dom
description: Query DOM elements by CSS selector, returning structure, attributes, bounding rect and, with properties, computed styles. Use it when you already have a selector (no match: count 0); to find one, get_interactives or find_text; for the rule that set a style, get_css_styles.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

name: get_css_styles
description: Why an element looks the way it does: for each CSS property the winning declaration — selector, stylesheet, rule position, !important, @layer, @media — and the ones it overrides, like the Styles panel of DevTools; query_dom gives the computed value, this gives who set it. Read-only, from the CSSOM: stylesheets of another origin without CORS are opaque and listed by href; user-agent styles, @container and @scope rules are not evaluated. properties narrows the output.

selector.description: CSS selector; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM. Only the first match is inspected

properties.description: Only these, e.g. ["margin-top","--brand"]; margin covers its longhands. Omitted = every property a matching rule sets

include_inherited.description: Also inherited properties (color, font-*, custom properties) with the ancestor that sets them

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

name: modify_dom
description: Change an element in the live DOM: setAttribute, removeAttribute, addClass, removeClass, setStyle, setTextContent. Nothing is persisted — the next reload restores the page as the server sends it. For styling many elements at once inject_css is one call instead of N.

selector.description: CSS selector; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM. Only the first match is changed

action.description: setStyle takes a CSS declaration in value; addClass/removeClass take className

value.description: Attribute value, style declaration, or text, per action

name: inject_css
description: Inject a CSS rule into the page. Stays until the next navigation or reload, and re-injecting the same id replaces it rather than stacking. Affects only what is rendered — the stylesheet of the site is untouched.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: read_console
description: Read console messages captured since page load, incl. uncaught errors and unhandled rejections. clear deletes the messages it returns, hence not read-only; since=cursor reads only newer ones without deleting, and failed requests are in monitor_network.

level.description: all merges every level in one chronological list

format.description: lines is compact; json keeps timestamps and stack traces

sourcemap.description: Resolve bundle.js:line:col frames to source files through their source maps

since.description: cursor from the previous read: only newer entries, nothing deleted

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: monitor_network
description: Monitor network requests. source=page: XHR/fetch hook (installed on first call); source=browser: all requests incl. static assets; source=websocket: connections and messages. format=har exports HAR 1.2. It only observes: to block, stub or rewrite requests use network_rules, to send one yourself http_request.

source.description: page: XHR/fetch only; browser: static assets too; websocket: connections and messages

format.description: har exports HAR 1.2 for external tooling

since.description: cursor from the previous read: only newer entries, nothing deleted

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: create_tab
description: Open a new tab, optionally at a URL, and make it the implicit target of later commands in this session. Each call creates another tab: reuse a tab_id or navigate() to move an existing one instead of piling up tabs.

active.description: false opens the tab in the background, leaving the current one focused

name: wait_for
description: Block until a condition holds: element, text, function (JS expression; needs the "Allow user scripts" toggle), navigation (mode=spa for client-side routes), network_idle. Polls until timeout (10s element/function, 15s the rest) then **returns `found: false` with a reason instead of raising**: check it, or a failed wait reads as success. Read-only.

condition.description: element and text need selector or text; function needs expression

selector.description: condition=element; with condition=text it narrows the search to that subtree

text.description: Literal text to wait for (condition=text), matched case-insensitively

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

name: scroll
description: Scroll. action=to: once to element/coordinates; action=until: repeatedly until element visible, network idle, or no new content (infinite scroll). It moves the tab's scroll position and returns it (to) or stopped_reason and steps (until); full_page_screenshot scrolls by itself, wait_for waits without scrolling.

action.description: to jumps to a position or element; until scrolls repeatedly to load more

selector.description: Target (to) or stop element (until=element)

x.description: Absolute horizontal position in px (action=to, without selector)

y.description: Absolute vertical position in px (action=to, without selector)

behavior.description: instant avoids waiting for smooth-scroll animations

until.description: no_new_content stops when the page height stops growing

max_scrolls.description: Cap on scroll steps, so an infinite feed terminates

step_px.description: px per step, default viewport height

container.description: until: selector that scrolls; default the document, or the largest scrollable element if the document does not scroll

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

name: set_storage
description: Write, delete or clear a localStorage/sessionStorage key, or a cookie with its path, domain and expiry. action=clear wipes every entry of that type for the origin and cannot be undone — on a site the user is logged into, clearing cookies logs them out. Read the current values first with get_storage.

type.description: cookie writes a real cookie, not a storage key

action.description: clear ignores key and wipes every entry of that type

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: fill_form
description: Batch fill form fields with React-compatible events. Handles input, select, checkbox, radio, and textarea. Fields and submit take a CSS selector or a ref (n1, n2…) from navigate/get_interactives. With submit_selector it also submits, so a repeated call submits twice — not safe to retry blindly; after a submit, after_submit carries url, title and the text the page gained (the confirmation or the errors). Each field reports value_after and mismatch; page_changed carries the DOM delta, and the refs of what appeared.

selector.description: CSS selector; ignored when ref is given

value.description: Text, option value or label; for checkbox/radio "true"/"false"

checked.description: Checkbox/radio instead of value: true checks, false unchecks

fields.description: {selector or ref, value or checked} per field

submit_selector.description: Submit button to click after filling

submit_ref.description: Submit button as a ref, instead of submit_selector

wait_after.description: Settle before returning: navigation waits for a page load, networkidle for quiet traffic

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

name: viewport_resize
description: Resize the Chrome **window** to a preset (mobile 375x812, tablet 768x1024, desktop 1440x900) or explicit dimensions; the viewport is smaller by the browser chrome, action=get reports the real one. width/height override half a preset. A maximized window on ChromeOS ignores the request.

action.description: get reports the current viewport without resizing anything

left.description: Window x on the virtual desktop; on multi-monitor this is what picks the screen

top.description: Window y on the virtual desktop

zoom.description: Page zoom for this origin, 1 = 100%; applied after the resize

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: element_screenshot
description: Screenshot cropped to one element or to a viewport region (PNG), optionally enlarged. Read-only. The cheapest image in the set, because it carries only the box you asked for — and with scale the way to read fine print: crop the box, zoom it, verify.

selector.description: CSS selector; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM. The element is scrolled into view first

region.description: Box in viewport CSS px (the rect frame of get_interactives/query_dom), instead of selector

scale.description: Enlargement of the crop, 1-4; output still capped at 1568px

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: full_page_screenshot
description: Full-page capture by scrolling: stitched segments of ~2 viewports (≤1568px), or one image per viewport with stitch=false. Expensive: ~2.7k image tokens per segment, only max_segments returned, the rest via segment_offset. Reading the text you need is cheaper by an order of magnitude — prefer read_page, extract or find_text unless layout is the question.

max_scrolls.description: Cap on scroll steps: a taller page is captured only up to here

max_segments.description: Images returned from the top (≈2.7k image tokens each); segment_offset for the rest

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: measure_spacing
description: Measure the gap, overlap and distance in CSS pixels between two elements, with their margins and paddings. Read-only. Values come from the current layout, so zoom and viewport size change them: viewport_resize({zoom:1}) and a fixed viewport_resize make results comparable across runs.

selector1.description: First element; distances are measured from its box

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: watch_dom
description: Watch DOM mutations (MutationObserver) under selector, to see what an action changed. First call installs the watcher in the page; later calls return the latest mutations (type, tag, attribute, nodes added/removed), clear deletes the ones returned, stop disconnects and empties the buffer. To wait for one element or text use wait_for.

selector.description: Subtree to observe; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM

subtree.description: Observe descendants too, not just the matched node

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: emulate_media
description: Make the page believe it runs elsewhere, until reset or reload: prefers-color-scheme, prefers-reduced-motion, print mode, navigator.userAgent/platform. user_agent changes only what page JS reads — the request header is network_rules modify_header. via "page" (default for these) only patches matchMedia and, for reduce, zeroes every animation: the site's own @media rules do not apply. via "debugger" emulates like DevTools, so the site's @media (prefers-reduced-motion) rules really apply — use it to check reduced motion with animations — and adds contrast, CPU throttling, network profiles, device viewport with DPR, touch (these imply via debugger). via debugger keeps Chrome's "started debugging this browser" bar until reset: true; in launch mode nobody sees it. Pair with viewport_resize to emulate a device in page mode.

printMode.description: Make print media queries match, without opening a print dialog

user_agent.description: Overrides navigator.userAgent and appVersion in the page (not the HTTP header)

via.description: page: script shim, no browser bar; debugger: real emulation (default when a debugger-only option is set)

cpu_throttle.description: CPU slowdown factor, e.g. 4 for a mid-range phone; 1 turns it off (debugger)

network.description: DevTools network profile; none turns it off (debugger)

mobile.description: Mobile viewport: meta viewport and overlay scrollbars apply

reset.description: Remove all emulations and detach the debugger

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: animations
description: List the page animations: CSS animations, transitions, Web Animations and View Transitions, each with selector and ref, animated properties, duration, delay, easing (linear() curves included), iterations, play state, timeline (document, scroll, view). composited_estimate guesses whether only transform/opacity/filter move (an estimate, not the compositor's answer); fade_only marks opacity-only fades, what prefers-reduced-motion should leave. Without duration_ms: what runs now. With duration_ms: records every animation that starts in the window, optionally after an action (hover, click, scroll, key), since a 150 ms transition is over before a second call. Refuses on a hidden page. Pair with emulate_media reducedMotion to check the reduced version; how smoothly they run is frames.

scope.description: CSS selector: only animations on this element or inside it

duration_ms.description: Record for this many ms (max 30000) instead of a snapshot

y.description: scroll without selector: absolute vertical position in px

trusted.description: Real browser input via chrome.debugger; default true for hover (CSS :hover needs it), false otherwise

name: frames
description: Record the page for duration_ms and report how smooth it ran: main-thread frame rate and dropped frames, Long Animation Frames (duration, blocking time, render and style/layout start, the scripts responsible), layout shifts with the elements that moved (CLS for the window only), and the slowest interaction (INP for the window, split into input delay, processing, presentation; needs trusted input, synthetic events have no interaction id). Optionally runs an action (click, hover, scroll, key) right after recording starts. Animations that started are counted too. Compositor-only animations can stay smooth while the main thread drops frames. Refuses on a hidden page: rAF and observers stop there. For load speed use perf_trace; for the settings of each animation, animations.

action.description: Action run right after recording starts

type.description: What to do once recording has started

selector.description: CSS selector of the element to act on (scroll: element to scroll into view)

y.description: scroll without selector: absolute vertical position in px

trusted.description: Real browser input via chrome.debugger; default true for hover (CSS :hover needs it), false otherwise

name: perf_trace
description: Record a DevTools performance trace and return its conclusions, never the trace: LCP with its phases (TTFB, resource load delay and duration, render delay), FCP, CLS (session windows), INP, the document request, render-blocking resources, long tasks with the function responsible, long animation frames. The raw trace goes to a JSON file (path and size in the result) that DevTools > Performance can load. action record (default) = start, reload unless reload: false, optional action, wait duration_ms, stop. start/stop bracket anything else done meanwhile. Uses chrome.debugger: Chrome shows its debugging bar while tracing; in launch mode nobody sees it. Refuses on a hidden page. For smoothness during an interaction use frames, for scores lighthouse.

reload.description: Reload the page right after tracing starts (default true for record, false for start)

duration_ms.description: record: how long to trace, max 60000

Chrome sends a frame only when the page changes; the video keeps the real timing. Needs the tab active and its window visible, and ffmpeg on the server machine (without it: the JPEG folder and the ffmpeg command). Uses chrome.debugger: Chrome shows its debugging bar while recording; in launch mode nobody sees it.

name: find_text
description: Find text on the page: parent selector, context, visibility, position per match. Attaches nearby interactive elements (with refs for click/type_text/hover) for the first visible match. Use it when you know the words on screen but not the selector (query_dom needs one); no match returns count 0.

name: network_rules
description: Network interception, browser-wide, survives reloads until cleared: block, redirect, set/remove headers, stub a synthetic body, or record real API responses and replay them with forced errors/latency (local helper; from HTTPS pages the stub host must be trusted). It changes traffic, while monitor_network only observes it and http_request sends one request; each rule comes back as added, list shows them, clear removes them all.

action.description: record saves the page's API responses (url_filter) as a fixture, replay serves them with overrides; list/clear

header_target.description: response = strip content-security-policy / x-frame-options, inject CORS

resource_types.description: Limit the rule to these request types; omitted = all of them

name: screenshot_diff
description: Visual regression: save a named baseline (viewport, element, or a PNG such as the design mockup) and compare later — changed-pixel % and a red-highlighted diff; or compare_urls: production vs staging in this tab, pixels plus text diff, logged-in pages included. Baselines are in-memory (lost on service worker restart).

action.description: baseline stores, compare measures against it, compare_urls diffs url_a vs url_b here, clear drops baselines

name.description: Baseline id: reuse the same one to compare across runs

selector.description: Capture one element (default viewport)

from_file.description: action=baseline: take it from this PNG (design mockup) instead of capturing

url_b.description: compare_urls: page under test, e.g. staging or a PR preview

mask.description: compare_urls: selectors hidden on both pages (dates, carousels, ads)

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: track_events
description: Decode the tracking beacons the page fired (GA4, Meta Pixel, Google Ads, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Microsoft Ads, GTM, Hotjar, Clarity) from the browser network log: one line per event with its key params. Read-only; POST-body params are flagged, not decoded.

name: cookie_audit

name: handoff
description: Hand the browser to the user for what only a person can do — 2FA, CAPTCHA, login, a choice — and wait: a banner in the page shows your message with Done/Cancel, the call returns on click or timeout, redirects included. pick_element: the user clicks an element and you get its selector. Never type credentials yourself. ask: the user types a reply in the banner ("which of the three?") and you get it as answer. pick_max: with pick_element, up to N elements; the user presses Done when finished.

message.description: What the user should do, one line

pick_element.description: Ask the user to click an element; returns its selector, text and box

pick_max.description: With pick_element: up to N elements, the user presses Done when finished

timeout.description: ms to wait for the click, default 5 min

in_terminal.description: Also ask in the Claude Code terminal (MCP elicitation) when the client supports it; the first answer wins. Not for pick_element

name: watch
description: Keep watching a page in the background — "tell me when the pipeline is green / the Approve button appears / this number changes" — checked every interval_s by the extension. Events are collected, not pushed: action=poll, or a script blocking on "chrome-bridge watch --wait <name>". Survives extension idling, not a browser restart. poll returns one line per event (time, name, kind, url, value, previous); a change due within seconds is wait_for.

action.description: poll = events since a timestamp

selector.description: Element that appears (until=match) or disappears (until=gone)

until.description: Default: change with value_of, else match

reload.description: Reload before each check, for pages that do not update live

since.description: poll: events after this ms timestamp

name: read_form
description: Read a form as the user filled it — label, type, value, checked/selected, required-but-empty, browser validity — to check it against the project's documents before an irreversible Submit. Password and card values come back [redacted]. Read-only, on request; to change values use fill_form.

name: audit
description: One-call page audit, pick the kinds: accessibility, keyboard (tab order and focus issues), SEO, security headers, broken links, Core Web Vitals, unused CSS, resources (which plugin/theme/module/host slows the page), cache (is the CDN serving the new version). A summary line per kind; with save_to the full Markdown report with every finding. Read-only. For one deep look at load speed use perf_trace, for Lighthouse scores lighthouse.

kinds.description: Default skips keyboard, css (slow, approximate), resources and cache

name: find_setting
description: Where is a setting in an unknown admin panel: follows the panel's menu links (same origin) until a page contains the keyword. Returns the URL, the menu path (Settings › Media) and the matching text; when nothing matches, how many pages it tried. Navigates the tab and leaves it on the last page visited, at most max_pages.

keyword.description: What you are looking for, e.g. "webp", "cron", "maintenance mode"

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: extract_table
description: Read a real <table> as JSON: thead cells become keys, each row an object. Only for tabular markup — `where` filters rows server-side, so one matching row out of 1500 costs a few hundred bytes instead of the whole document. `row_count` is the table total, `match_count` how many rows passed the filter. No table at index is an error saying how many the selector found; for cards and lists use extract.

selector.description: The table to read; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM

index.description: Which table to take when the selector matches several, 0-based

max_rows.description: Max rows returned to you (output cap).

where.description: {column: substring} rows must match, case-insensitive (names too). Key "any" matches any cell.

columns.description: Return only these columns per row.

offset.description: Skip N rows of the (filtered) set before applying max_rows.

scan_rows.description: Max rows materialized in-page to scan/filter; raise for very large tables.

name: drag_and_drop
description: Drag an element onto another. html5 = DragEvent+DataTransfer; pointer = pointer/mouse events (sortable libraries). It scrolls the source into view and returns once the events are sent, without knowing whether the app accepted the drop (check with assert or query_dom); a missing element is an error.

description: Read or write the system clipboard (text). Activates the tab and focuses its window first. write overwrites whatever the user had copied, which is not recoverable. To fill a field use type_text instead of write and paste; read checks what a Copy button copied, and an empty clipboard returns text "".

name: set_geolocation
description: Override navigator.geolocation with fixed coordinates (page-level patch). reset restores native. For location-based pages (store locators, delivery zones): it answers without a permission prompt, and a reload or navigation drops it, so call it after navigate.

name: manage_downloads
description: List downloads, start one, or wait for the newest to finish. Files land in the browser Downloads folder, not on the server. download reports the real state: with Chrome set to ask where to save, it comes back waiting_for_user — bytes fetched, nothing moves until someone picks a destination. To save a file that has a URL use http_request with save_to instead: browser cookies, bytes on disk, no dialog; a file the page builds goes through capture_downloads.

action.description: download fetches with the browser cookies and reports the real state; wait_for_complete blocks until the newest finishes

url.description: What to download (action=download); sent with the session cookies of its origin

filename.description: Relative path inside the Downloads folder (action=download)

limit.description: Max download entries returned, newest first

name: capture_downloads
description: Save files the page builds itself, with no browser download and no "Save as" dialog: blob and data URL links (a[download]), window.showSaveFilePicker writes, and downloads the page starts (cancelled at once, bytes fetched again with the browser cookies). arm with save_dir, then click Export/Download, then wait: it returns the saved paths. A file with a URL: http_request save_to instead. Names are cleaned, existing files never overwritten, size capped by max_mb.

action.description: arm before the click; wait returns what arrived and stays armed; disarm restores the page

save_dir.description: arm: absolute directory for the files; created if missing

max_mb.description: arm: per-file cap in MB (default 100, max 200); a bigger file is skipped

timeout.description: wait: max ms for the first file

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: save_page
description: Save the full page (DOM, styles, images) as an MHTML archive file on the server filesystem. An offline copy Chrome reopens as it looked, for evidence or a later comparison (for an image use screenshot, for the text read_page); it overwrites output_path and returns path and size.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

name: http_request
description: HTTP request sent from the browser, with the logged-in user's cookies: fetches what a server-side request gets a login page for (invoices, authenticated JSON, exports). Text bodies inline (capped by max_length); save_to writes the bytes — the way to read a PDF, since read_page returns nothing on a PDF tab, and the way to save any file that has a URL: no click on Download, no browser download, no "Save as" dialog.

url.description: Absolute URL. Cookies are sent for its origin

method.description: HEAD fetches headers only, without the body

save_to.description: Absolute path: write the response bytes here instead of returning them (PDF, images, archives)

max_length.description: Max chars of body returned inline

name: move_tab
description: Move an existing tab into another window (chrome.tabs.move), keeping id, history and page state; works on chrome-untrusted:// tabs too. The **destination** must be a normal window: out of an app/popup window is fine, into one is refused. A ChromeOS Terminal tab can be pulled out (new_window, window_type popup) but never merged back: extensions cannot create app windows.

tab_id.description: Tab to move; get it from get_tabs

window_id.description: Destination window; get_tabs reports windowId for every tab

new_window.description: Extract the tab into a fresh window instead of an existing one

window_type.description: new_window only: popup has no tab strip nor omnibox, the terminal-window look

index.description: Position in the destination window; -1 appends at the end

name: tile_windows
description: Tile Chrome windows over one monitor in equal parts with no gap. Only Chrome windows. The monitor is the one of a window already on it, whose work area is read from a page there: at least one target needs a scriptable tab (not chrome://). Maximized windows are restored first, since maximized ignores bounds. To restore a saved arrangement use window_layout; to move one tab into another window, move_tab.

window_ids.description: Windows to tile; omitted = every normal window on the reference monitor

reference_window_id.description: Window whose monitor is used; omitted = the focused one

layout.description: columns splits left to right, rows top to bottom, grid keeps tiles as square as it can

padding.description: Px of empty margin kept inside the work area

include_types.description: Window types to include; omitted = normal only

area.description: Monitor area to fill, when no target window has a scriptable tab to read it from

name: window_layout
description: Save the current window arrangement under a name, restore, list or delete. save overwrites silently. Window ids do not survive a browser restart: restore matches windows by the overlap of their tab URLs and reports the ones it cannot recognise instead of guessing.

action.description: save snapshots every window; restore repositions the recognised ones

name.description: Layout name, required except for list

name: http_auth
description: Set/clear credentials for HTTP Basic/Digest auth dialogs (browser-wide, in-memory only).

action.description: set installs credentials for HTTP auth prompts; clear removes them

password.description: Required for action=set; kept in memory, never written to disk

name: session_fixture
description: Snapshot localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies of the current origin into a named fixture (a logged-in state, usually), restore one, or list them. save overwrites silently; restore writes on top without clearing and refuses on a different origin — cookies would attach to the wrong site.

action.description: save snapshots the current origin; restore writes it back

description: Run a WebMCP tool the page declares (see webmcp_tools or the webmcp line of navigate): one call instead of the clicks and fields it replaces. Returns status (ok, error, timeout, not_found, inactive, needs_confirmation), the tool result and ms; navigated_to when the call led to another page. A sensitive tool (buy, pay, send, delete, a POST form) is not run without confirm:true: on needs_confirmation ask the user, then repeat with confirm.

name: extract
description: Read repeated non-tabular structures — product cards, list items, search results — as one record per item: item_selector matches the repeating block, fields map output names to selectors relative to it. Read-only, deterministic, parsed server-side from the main-document HTML. Default output: total and shown, then one tab-separated row per item under the field names; a field with no match is empty (null in json).

name: assert
description: Assert a page condition, polling until timeout: element exists/visible (optionally with count or containing text), text on page, tab url/title. Patterns: substring, or "/…/" for regex. Recorded flows replay it as a test. Unlike wait_for, which returns found: false, a failure is an error naming what did not match; success returns passed and waited_ms.

name: session_record
description: Record the commands of this session as a replayable jsonl (chrome-bridge replay --file <path>); observe what the user does in a tab ("watch how I do it") into the same format plus a readable procedure, never recording sensitive values; export a recording as a Playwright test for CI. Replays target the tab they navigate. Use it for a flow to repeat or a procedure to hand over; for one check now, assert.
